resources.string: Geiger counter for poor mobile data. Pings run on cellular only. Tune each alert sound below; media volume buttons still apply.
No cellular connection available. Disable Wi‑Fi or enable mobile data.

Reception LED from RSRP/RSRQ: green above −95 dBm, yellow −105 to −95 dBm, red below −105 dBm or RSRQ below −18 dB. RSRP at or below −125 dBm triggers the no-signal tone. Alert tones follow the same signal rules.

Clicks speed up when RTT, jitter, or packet loss worsen. Low-signal clicks follow RSRP/RSRQ tiers (5 s / 2.5 s / 1 s / 0.5 s). Limited service uses a two-tone alert, or 300 ms on/off on 2G with no home GSM. No signal is pulsed unless you are completely out of service with no SOS on any SIM — then it stays continuous.
Shows when NotSpotter is measuring mobile data quality.
Monitoring paused after running 6h in the background — open the app to resume it.
Active ping tests stopped after 10 minutes. Signal alert sounds and KPI polling continue until you tap Stop.
Signal-only monitoring — no ping tests. Low-signal click rates follow your passive signal range settings. Alert audio continues until you tap Stop.
Passive-only monitoring — RSRP, EARFCN, and PCI continue updating. Tap Stop to end monitoring.
Passive signal thresholds and alert settings
Tap to set RXSS tier boundaries, signal pulse sounds, and per-state voice and alert tones for passive monitoring.
Speaks “signal low” on entry and every 30 s while in RXSS 5 on LTE/NR. Same setting as RXSS 6 and 2G weak (RXSS 8). Voice only — no alert tone.
Speaks “signal low” on entry and every 30 s while in signal low (RXSS 6) on LTE/NR. Same setting as RXSS 5 and 2G weak (RXSS 8). Voice only — no alert tone.
RSRP above −125 dBm through the RXSS 5 lower boundary (fixed)
Momentary alert on LTE, NR, or 2G cell reselect (channel, PCI, or BSIC change). Applies on any camped technology.
After the cell change bell, speaks operator, technology, then cell reselect with channel and PCI/BSIC (e.g. “E E, 4 G, cell reselect, channel 6 4 0 0, PCI 1 2 3”).
Momentary alert when the camped technology becomes 2G. Voice speaks only the new technology (e.g. “E E, 2 G”).
After the sweep tone, speaks the operator name then “2 G”. Also used for the 2G camp reminder after LTE/NR loss.
Momentary alert when the camped technology becomes LTE (4G). Voice speaks only the new technology (e.g. “E E, 4 G”).
After the sweep tone, speaks the operator name then “4 G”.
Momentary alert when the camped technology becomes NR standalone or EN-DC. Voice speaks only the new technology (e.g. “E E, 5 G E N D C”).
After the sweep tone, speaks the operator name then “5 G” or “5 G E N D C”.
Speaks “signal low” on entry and every 30 s while on 2G weak (RXSS 8). Same setting as RXSS 5 and signal low (RXSS 6) on LTE/NR. Voice only — no alert tone.
Used by signal high (RXSS 1), RXSS 2, and signal low (RXSS 6). Also under Global alert sound settings.
Shared with the global signal pulse duration under Global alert sound settings.
Volume and frequency shared by RXSS 2–5. Each tier below keeps its own enable toggle, RSRP boundary, pulse duration, and click interval.
Tone and voice settings are shared with LTE/NR no signal (RXSS 10), searching 2G (RXSS 11), home 2G no signal (RXSS 15), and WiFi calling no signal (RXSS 31).
Tone and voice settings are shared with dead zone (RXSS 0), searching 2G (RXSS 11), home 2G no signal (RXSS 15), visited 4G no signal overlay (RXSS 20), and WiFi calling no signal (RXSS 31).
Tone and voice settings are shared with LTE/NR no signal (RXSS 10), dead zone (RXSS 0), home 2G no signal (RXSS 15), and WiFi calling no signal (RXSS 31).
Tone and voice settings are shared with visited operator 2G limited service (RXSS 13). No-signal overlay RXSS 20 uses LTE/NR no signal (RXSS 10) tone and voice.
Tone and voice settings are shared with visited operator limited service (RXSS 12). No-signal overlay RXSS 23 uses home 2G no signal (RXSS 15) tone and voice.
Tone and voice settings are shared with LTE/NR no signal (RXSS 10), dead zone (RXSS 0), searching 2G (RXSS 11), visited 2G no signal overlay (RXSS 23), and WiFi calling no signal (RXSS 31).
Tone and voice settings are shared with LTE/NR no signal (RXSS 10), dead zone (RXSS 0), searching 2G (RXSS 11), and home 2G no signal (RXSS 15).
How often RSRP, RSRQ, and cell identity are refreshed during passive monitoring (1–10 s).

RXSS 1 (signal high) sits above RXSS 2–5 (highest RSRP to lowest). RXSS 6 (signal low) spans above −125 dBm through the RXSS 5 boundary. RXSS 2–5 share pulse sound and click interval; each tier keeps its own enable toggle and RSRP boundary.
Plays every %1$d ms (raised to fit signal pulse duration)
Interval is more than twice your %1$d s measurement cycle — signal tier may change before the next click.
Mock network state active — metrics come from the selected scenario, not the live radio. Switch scenarios or drag sliders while running to test tiers, voice, and tones.
Simulate camp states during passive-only monitoring to test tiers, voice alerts, and tones without live signal.
Requires passive-only (mock signal) start. One scenario at a time.
Pick the network camp state to simulate.
No service and searching scenarios ignore RSRP/RSRQ. Values are kept for when you switch to a camped scenario.
On 2G scenarios, mock RSRP drives the RX level tier; RSRQ is stored but not reported on 2G.
Requires “All technologies (include 2G)” enabled. Allow two measurement cycles for the Searching 2G tier to appear.
In service on home 4G — RXSS 1–6 from mock RSRP/RSRQ.
Camped on home 2G — RXSS 7–8 from mock RX level.
Limited service on visited operator 4G — limited-service tier and tone.
Limited service on visited operator 2G — no home GSM; visited-operator 2G pulse.
Out of service on all technologies — RXSS 0 dead zone.
4G lost, scanning for home 2G — Searching 2G tier and voice after 5 s.
In service on home 5G NSA (EN-DC, LTE anchor + NR) — RXSS 1–6 from mock RSRP/RSRQ; technology-change voice announces “5 G E N D C”.
In service via WiFi calling only, no cellular RAT/RSRP — RXSS 31, “WiFi calling, no cellular signal” voice.
Used instead of RXSS 1–6 when 2G fallback is enabled and the phone is on 2G. Split at %1$d dBm: RXSS 7 at or above, RXSS 8 below.
2G only — RX level at or above %1$d dBm
Home 2G camp, debounced no signal — separate from LTE/NR RXSS 10
Used when there is no signal from any network or technology (out of service everywhere, no limited service). RXSS 0 clicks replace the continuous flatline tone when enabled.
Camp states during not-spot hunting (RXSS 10, 15, 11, 12, 13). Each block has signal pulses and, where applicable, voice and alert tone controls below.
LTE/NR no signal (debounced) — not yet searching or dead zone
In service via WiFi calling (VoWiFi), no cellular RAT camped, no RSRP/RSRQ (debounced)
Scanning for home 2G after LTE/NR loss (all-tech mode)
Limited service on home or visited operator 4G
Click interval cannot be shorter than this duration plus 25 ms.
Complete dead zone — no signal on any technology
Signal range is fixed from %1$d to %2$d dBm. Drag each boundary to divide the tiers.
Fair boundary range is %1$d to %2$d dB. One boundary splits poor/critical from fair.
Tier 6 RSRQ: %1$d to %2$d dB · Tier 4+ RSRQ: %3$d to %4$d dB
Mix white noise into RSRP tier clicks
When enabled, RXSS 14 white noise is blended into your RSRP signal-pulse clicks. When disabled, RXSS 14 plays its own white-noise pulses on a separate schedule.
Active when RSRQ is below %1$d dB (fair boundary above).
RXSS 14 audio applies during passive-only monitoring.
Tap to tune when Geiger clicks speed up. Changes apply immediately, including while running in the background.
No Geiger clicks after a good test. Degraded, poor, flatline, and weak-signal clicks still play.
When a test rates as good connection, play this many clicks once per test cycle. Degraded and poor connections still use faster interval clicking.
Running as a foreground service. You can leave the app or lock the screen.
Battery optimization may pause monitoring. Allow unrestricted background use for reliable results.

Android requires location permission to read EARFCN and PCI. The app does not track your GPS position. After allowing location for NotSpotter, turn on the device Location toggle if EARFCN/PCI still show “Location needed”.
Configure the probe target, test interval, and pings per test.
The first ping in each test warms up the radio link (RRC) and is excluded; remaining pings are averaged for RTT.
How often a new ping test runs on cellular mobile data.
Choose which SIM to monitor and optional fallback behaviour.
Signal KPIs and ping tests use the selected SIM. Monitoring restarts automatically when you change SIM.
Phone permission needed to list SIM cards.

When enabled, monitors 2G fallback after 4G/5G loss: announces searching, reads 2G KPIs (RXSS 7–8), and treats visited-operator limited 2G/4G as usable service. When disabled, 2G is treated as no signal.

During passive-only monitoring, mute signal-tier clicks, cell-change bell, technology-change tone, and limited-service tone unless there is no signal, RSRQ is below %1$d dB, or RSRP is at or below %2$d dBm. The no-signal tone is always played.
Unmute passive alerts when RSRP or RSRQ cross these limits (used when quiet passive alerts is enabled).
Monitoring continues in the background via the persistent notification. Swiping the app away will not stop it. Per-sound volume sliders multiply the media stream level.
−70 to −126 dBm · 5 dB bins · active bins only
Voice announcer, connection-test clicks, shared signal-pulse loudness, and cell-change alerts. Per-RXSS voice and tones are under Passive signal thresholds and alert settings.
Stop monitoring to use Test buttons.
Tier click intervals in Passive signal thresholds and signal pulse settings cannot be shorter than this duration plus 25 ms. Increasing duration may raise tier intervals automatically.

Master switch for all spoken voice announcements. Turning this off mutes every voice announcement without changing your individual voice settings below; tones, bells, clicks, and vibration are unaffected.
After the cell change bell, speaks operator, technology, then cell reselect with channel and PCI (e.g. “E E, 4 G, cell reselect, channel 6 4 0 0, PCI 1 2 3”).

On cell reselect, after the technology name, say the E-UTRA band derived from the LTE channel (EARFCN) instead of “cell reselect, channel …, PCI …”. Falls back to the normal phrasing when there is no LTE channel to map (e.g. 2G-only reselect).
Speaks the E-UTRA band number as a whole number, e.g. “band, twenty” for band 20.
Speaks the band’s common MHz nickname as a whole number, e.g. “band, L eight hundred” for band 20 (L800).
After the sweep tone, speaks the network name and new radio technology (e.g. “E E, Technology change, 4 G”). Only when 2G, 4G, or 5G changes.

Speaks 5 seconds after signal enters RXSS 5, then every 30 seconds while RXSS 5 continues (e.g. “E E, 4 G, signal low”). On 2G fallback, RXSS 8 (2G weak) uses the same “signal low” voice every 30 seconds instead of the “2 G” camp reminder. Voice only — no alert tone.
Vibrates in sync with the no-signal tone when signal is lost, restored, or during periodic no-signal reminders.

After the no-signal tone, speaks when signal is lost or restored (e.g. “E E, 4 G, no signal” / “E E, 4 G, signal restored”). Dead zone: “deadzone, no service, no SOS calls”. WiFi calling: “E E, wifi calling, no cellular signal” / “E E, cellular signal restored”.

After the limited-service tone, speaks when emergency-only service starts (e.g. “Vodafone UK, E E, 4 G, limited service”). Repeats every 30 s while active, including when the camped operator changes. Returning to normal 4G/5G service is not announced — that is assumed.
Choose the text-to-speech voice used for all voice announcements.

Save and load named sets of app settings as JSON files on device storage. Use Export to Downloads for a file you can import later from the Downloads/NotSpotter folder. Profiles survive clearing app cache and can be shared with others. Saved profiles must differ from factory defaults.

A profile with this name already exists.
